recent_posts.title: #86 Golang - How to Emit Socket.IO Events from Golang
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to implement real-time communication in web applications using Socket.IO with Golang. This guide covers setting up a Socket.IO server with NodeJS, creating a client, and using a Golang service to emit events through Redis, enabling real-time capabilities without direct WebSocket connections.

recent_posts.title: #85 Golang - Functional Programming: First-Class Functions, Closures & More!
recent_posts.summary: This post provides an in-depth look at functional programming in Golang, focusing on first-class functions, higher-order functions, and closures. Examples are provided to demonstrate how functions can be treated as variables, passed as arguments, and returned from other functions. The concept of closures, where functions retain access to their environment, is also discussed through practical examples.

recent_posts.title: #84 Golang - Concurrency in Go Web Applications: From net/http to Background Workers
recent_posts.summary: Discover how concurrency works in Go web applications, focusing on the use of goroutines and channels. Learn about the concurrency model in Go's net/http and Gin frameworks, and understand best practices for handling background tasks efficiently. Explore the advantages of using established background processing systems like Factory, Async, or RabbitMQ for managing heavy operations.

recent_posts.title: #83 Golang - Advanced API Testing: Table-Driven Tests & Build Tags
recent_posts.summary: Explore advanced API testing techniques in Golang with table-driven tests and build tags. Learn how to structure test cases for better readability and manage tests using build tags to separate unit, smoke, and integration tests. This method ensures efficient testing without duplicating code.

recent_posts.title: #82 Golang - API Rate Limiting (Revised) | Prevent API Abuse
recent_posts.summary: This post revisits the concept of API rate limiting in Golang, emphasizing the use of the rate package. It addresses a previous mistake by introducing a mutex for concurrent access and demonstrates how to implement a rate limiter to control the frequency of API requests using the token bucket algorithm. An example implementation includes setting up middleware to handle rate limiting based on IP addresses, employing sync.Map for improved concurrency handling, and testing the solution to ensure its effectiveness.

recent_posts.title: #81 Golang - Observability: Logging with Loki, Alloy & Grafana
recent_posts.summary: Enhance observability in Golang applications by setting up logging using Loki and Grafana. Use Alloy to collect logs and send them to Loki, then visualize and analyze logs in Grafana. Details on setting up Grafana, configuring SLOG for logging, and steps to integrate logs from Alloy to Loki are provided along with some basic operations you can perform in Grafana.

recent_posts.title: Golang TCP and UDP Sockets Guide
recent_posts.summary: Discover how to build simple TCP and UDP servers and clients using Go. Learn the basics of network programming with practical examples, such as how to create an echo server, handle connections, and manage timeouts for non-blocking communication. Stay tuned for more Go programming tutorials.

recent_posts.title: #79 Golang - Observability: Logging with Loki, Promtail & Grafana
recent_posts.summary: Enhance observability in Golang applications by setting up logging using Loki, Promtail, and Grafana. Learn how to collect and send logs to Loki with Promtail and visualize them in Grafana. The post explains the setup process, configuring a Go application to write logs, using Promtail for log collection, and using Grafana to visualize and analyze logs.

recent_posts.title: #78 Golang - REST API Calls with Resty
recent_posts.summary: The post dives into using the Resty package in Golang for making REST API calls more efficiently. By comparing Resty to Go's net HTTP package, it highlights Resty's fluent API, handling of retries and timeouts, and automatic JSON marshalling/unmarshalling. The post includes a demonstration of building a CRUD API with Go using Resty, showcasing code snippets for creating, reading, updating, and deleting tasks in a task management API.

recent_posts.title: #77 Golang - API Rate Limiting | Prevent API Abuse
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to implement rate limiting for APIs using Golang's rate package. The guide includes setting up an HTTP server, creating middleware to manage request limits, and handling requests based on IP addresses. This implementation provides a basic framework for protecting APIs from abuse and ensuring fair resource allocation.
